body:
Scope and classification: isolated formal Proposal Review, manual execution, direction-level assessment of the complete Design-Derived Test Model proposal. Explicit rigorloop-records-v2 primary recording replaces historical Markdown review/log and settlement mechanics. Scope-budget context applies because model/consumer alignment and existing-suite cleanup are separate workstreams. Vision-exception and missing-standing-artifact predicates are false; no bootstrap or automation is involved.

Review dimensions:
- Challenge: pass. The proposal identifies weak derivation, redundant cases and obsolete expectations as the problem without falsely claiming that an audit has already identified useless repository tests.
- Goals: pass. Design-derived objectives/outcomes and removal or consolidation of demonstrably unnecessary tests are both outcome-oriented, with regression and failure-path protection retained.
- Scope: pass. The scope table makes model ownership core, consumer alignment a same-slice dependency, and actual audit/cleanup an included separate implementation slice. Blanket historical conversion is excluded. Inventory and bounded suite selection are explicit Delivery obligations rather than hidden deferral or arbitrary deletion authority.
- Governing principle: pass. Every test protects an engineering obligation and every removal accounts for remaining or retired protection; the principle is independent of tooling.
- Direction: pass. One Test model owns purpose, derivation, protective-value and maintenance criteria. Product/component Design remains behavioral authority; Delivery allocates proof; implementation owns test mechanics. Specialist reviewers and Verify assess actual subjects/evidence. Review and Closeout retains assessment authority, independence, judgment, applicability and closeout policy. This expressly preserves the user's latest clarification and avoids making the Test model a runtime approver.
- Feasibility: pass. Exactly one embedded Feasibility assessment cites existing plan requirement-to-proof allocation, boundary/negative-case derivation and RC evidence policy. Direct inspection supports those references. A policy extraction and consumer refactor is credible enough for Design, while concrete cleanup feasibility remains bounded by inventory and retained-protection assessment. No specific deletion or measured saving is claimed.
- Material impact: pass. Maintenance overhead and risk of losing undocumented regression knowledge are disclosed; group-level rationale, semantic review and investigation of uncertain protection keep the direction proportionate.
- Vision alignment: pass; aligned. VISION.md values traceable requirements, concrete proof and reviewable decisions, and rejects code volume without evidence. The proposal strengthens that chain while avoiding per-function administrative obligations and platform migration.
- Downstream authority: pass. Ownership reconciliation, representative acceptance examples, exact cleanup candidates, implementation mechanics and automation remain Design/Delivery work. Randomized/property testing and regression-discovered Design gaps are preserved rather than prohibited by a rigid preexisting-label rule.
- Requested decision: pass. Approval supports detailed Design only, explicitly withholding specific deletions, final relocation, layout, implementation, migration and activation.

Scope-preservation result: both original goals are visible in Goals, Scope and Decision requested. Tests derive from approved Design or an explicit justified engineering obligation; arbitrary case multiplication is challenged. Removal of unnecessary/useless cases remains in the initiative, with evidence obligations appropriate to deletion risk. Lack of requirement labels, runtime cost, similar names and passing validation are explicitly insufficient removal grounds. The latest authority clarification is incorporated without taking away actual assessment responsibility from specialists or Verify.

Specialized scope-budget gate: pass. Model policy, consumer alignment and cleanup have explicit treatment and boundaries. Repository-wide automatic conversion is excluded with a clear rationale; no hidden future work or unanswered direction-level ownership decision prevents this assessment. No proposal edits are required to make the direction decision responsible. Detailed cleanup completion bounds must be selected before implementation, as the proposal already requires; that downstream task is not a missing proposal-level audit.

Evidence and limits: read the complete proposal, VISION.md, applicable Constitution and model ownership boundaries, linked plan quality contract and boundary verification reference. These bounded sources were necessary to verify the proposal's feasibility and non-conflicting policy ownership, not to preapprove Test-model Design. Current primary context is complete for proposal/review/findings/blockers/applicability and reveals no prior unresolved concern. All relied-on files were mechanically inspected for exact identity before recording. No test suite was audited, no case judged redundant, no deletion approved, and no implementation or final proof adequacy claimed.

Recording this direction assessment does not settle routing or begin Design. Return control to the caller at the isolated review boundary; Design may be pursued only under the user's separate continuation authority.
independence_basis: Separate delegated agent /root/independent_proposal_review reviewed this proposal without authoring or editing it. codex-author drafted the proposal from user direction and clarification; this execution independently read the complete subject and governing/linked evidence and writes only assessment evidence. Earlier work by this reviewer concerned independent assessments of a different initiative, not authorship of this proposal.
